name: Particle Art
visualIdentity: Recognizable subjects emerge from particle density, size, brightness, and color against a contrasting field. Selected trails suggest direction; coordinated poses, flows, and structural changes create the motion. Hold stable silhouettes at key moments and limit glow so detail remains visible.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to abstract brand moments and silhouette transformations. It can support data stories when particles represent real units, title reveals when paired with crisp type, and abstract or spatial passages. These are inferred applications; use only where particles carry meaning.
limitations: Dense text is hard to read during travel; particles alone should not carry long copy. Avoid unplanned hidden resets, excessive glow, and motion that undermines orientation or reduced-motion needs. Data counts must be truthful. Orb deformation is not proof of physical fluid behavior; do not imply unverified scientific relationships.
palette: Suggested tokens for new art only: background #111C29, foreground #EFF5EE, accent 1 #65BEC2, accent 2 #CEAF79. Use discrete colors; gradients are disabled. Task, brand, approved reference, and existing semantic colors take precedence; preserve exact values, roles, color families, and asset colors. Text contrast checks are candidates only; inspect actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Use fixed point samples, colors, and target poses; animate position and brightness with controlled blending and selective bloom. Keep important silhouettes steady for reading. Video motion must be deterministic and seekable from composition time. Interactive HTML may map finite scroll progress to states; support backward/direct state evaluation, keyboard/touch as applicable, and reduced motion. Do not add generic bounce or smoothing by default.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or required layer. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience, honoring supplied audio requirements and assets. Synchronize picture and sound; check speech clarity, balance, clipping, and timing.
assetRequirements: Requires authored or generated particle samples, colors, and target poses; cache or deterministically reproduce stateful simulations. Text should remain real DOM/SVG type for legibility and accessibility. For data, provide verified units and a data-table mirror. Load local fonts and assets; missing source assets are unspecified.
combinations: Use alone for abstract brand moments and silhouette transformations. Pair with data mapping and labels (style-097) when quantities matter, or typography (style-093) for short titles; keep labels clear and formed words held for reading time. Optional motion patterns fit only when their geometry and narrative are supported; no motion reference is required.
productionApproach: Choose the renderer and motion method for visual fidelity first: Three.js Points/BufferGeometry with GLSL can form and animate particle fields; Canvas 2D is an alternative. Keep visual construction, motion, and export responsibilities separate. HyperFrames is the default composition/export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, and record why. Make state reproducible, inspect key frames and the decoded result, and validate timing, dimensions, audio, and loop seams.
